question_en:
While organizing a box of old kitchen items left by my family, I discovered the five glass objects with the same pattern shown in the attached photo. They differ in shape and size, and I need to create an itemized list based on official records.

1. Based on the common decorative pattern on the surfaces of the five glass objects in the attachment, identify the pattern name. Then, using official museum collection records, state the name used for this pattern in the collection records, as well as the manufacturer, manufacturing location, and production date range for these objects.

2. Create a five-row table following the order "top row from left to right, bottom row from left to right" as shown in the photo. Each row must include the object name from the collection records, nominal capacity, museum accession number, and the height, width, and depth or diameter recorded on the museum page.

Answer Format: Please answer in two parts labeled (1) and (2). Each part should only address the corresponding sub-question and provide all required information for that question. Answer part (1) in text. For part (2), provide a five-row table in the order "top row from left to right, bottom row from left to right".
answer:
(1) Pattern Name in the Collection Records: Snowflake Blue (commonly known as Garland); Manufacturer: Corning Glass Works, Charleroi; Manufacturing Location: United States, PA, Charleroi; Production Date: 1972–1975.

(2)

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · P2-8-2-G01

## Step 01 · Start search from the common pattern on the five objects

Action: Observe the blue-and-white small snowflakes, dots, and continuous swags in the current image; first identify the pattern, then distinguish the object shapes. Example query: Pyrex blue snowflakes dots swags Garland Corning Museum.

Evidence observation: The five objects with the same pattern differ in size and shape; they cannot be matched as a single object just because the color is the same. The pattern name must be confirmed by the museum's Pattern Library, rather than using sellers' common nicknames as the final name.

Evidence links:
https://pyrex.cmog.org/pattern-library/snowflake-blue
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/collections/1223/pyrex

Result of this step: Enter the Pyrex system of the Corning Museum of Glass.

## Step 02 · Confirm the official pattern name and nickname

Action: Read the name, description, Date Introduced, and Manufactured dates on the Snowflake Blue pattern page.

Evidence observation: The official pattern name and collection title are Snowflake Blue, commonly known as Garland; the pattern description includes snowflakes, swags, and dots. Date Introduced is 1972, and the production date range is 1972–1975. The nickname can be noted in parentheses but does not replace the official name.

Evidence links:
https://pyrex.cmog.org/pattern-library/snowflake-blue

Result of this step: Candidates for the name and date range for Question 1 are determined.

## Step 03 · Exclude early similar snowflake patterns

Action: Separately check the Snowflake (Turquoise on White) entry, compare its pattern and year, and cross-verify along its reference to the 1972 Snowflake Blue description.

Evidence observation: The early Snowflake (Turquoise on White) was produced in 1956–1963; it is not the 1972 pattern combining small snowflakes, dots, and swags for this question. Similar color does not allow applying the 1956–1963 range to these five objects.

Evidence links:
https://pyrex.cmog.org/pattern-library/snowflake-turquoise-white
https://pyrex.cmog.org/pattern-library/snowflake-blue

Result of this step: Exclude date mismatches caused by similarly named patterns.

## Step 04 · Fix five position slots according to the input image

Action: Return to the current input and establish an order solely for matching: top row left → center → right, bottom row left → right.

Evidence observation: The five positions are respectively a small square box with a transparent lid, a shallow rectangular dish, a deeper blue rectangular dish, a handled mug, and a round bowl. The question image is used to identify shapes and order; nominal capacity, date, and dimensions must come from official records and cannot be estimated from photo proportions.

Evidence links:
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/objects/38209
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/objects/42854/
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/objects/37629/
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/objects/38223/snowflake-blue
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/objects/66583/snowflake-blue

Result of this step: Each position corresponds to one object record subsequently, and the final table maintains the same order.

## Step 05 · Match top row left: lidded small refrigerator dish

Action: Query Snowflake Blue refrigerator dish; read the object name, appearance description, and accession number for object38209.

Evidence observation: Name = 1-1/2 Cup Pyrex Refrigerator Dish; a white 1.5 cup small box with a handle and a transparent embossed lid, matching the top row left. Accession number 2010.4.407 C; capacity is explicitly given as 1-1/2 cup by the object name, no visual guessing needed.

Evidence links:
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/objects/38209
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/internal/media/dispatcher/180816/preview

Result of this step: Object and capacity for the first row are determined.

## Step 06 · Read dimensions for the small box and retain the object context including the lid

Action: Transcribe the Size field for 38209 in the Overall H/W/D order to avoid swapping length, width, and height positions.

Evidence observation: Height 8.2 cm, Width 10.7 cm, Depth 8.5 cm; this record includes both Opalware Glass and Glass, and the appearance description explicitly mentions a transparent lid. Dimensions follow the overall collection record and are not re-measured from the scene image.

Evidence links:
https://glasscollection.cmog.org/objects/38209

Result of this step: Dimensions for the first row are H 8.2, W 10.7, D 8.5.

## Step 07 · Match top row center: shallow rectangular dish

Action: Query 1-1/2 Pint Pyrex Dish; verify the white background with blue pattern and shallower shape for object42854.

Evidence observation: Name = 1-1/2 Pint Pyrex Dish; capacity 1-1/2 pint; accession number 2010.4.402; H 6.6, W 19.3, D 15.7 cm. This page does not list a transparent lid for this dish; do not copy the lid feature from the left-side box.

Action: Query 1 Quart Pyrex Dish; verify the blue exterior and white snowflake decoration for object37629.

Evidence observation: Name = 1 Quart Pyrex Dish; capacity 1 quart; accession number 2010.4.401; H 8.2, W 19.2, D 15.7 cm. Its width is close to the previous dish, but height and capacity differ; do not merge these two collection records.

## Step 09 · Match bottom row left: handled coffee mug

Action: Open object38223; verify the Pyrex Coffee Mug name, white background with blue pattern, accession number, and dimensions.

Evidence observation: Name = Pyrex Coffee Mug; accession number 2010.4.416 D; H 8.6, W 11.3, Diam 8.8 cm. This page provides two different fields for width and diameter; both should be retained; the object name itself does not directly state the capacity.

## Step 10 · Supplement the mug with a well-supported 9 oz capacity

Action: Return to the Snowflake Blue series object list, check the Mug entry, and connect it to the object page shape.

Evidence observation: The museum's series list explicitly lists 9 oz. Mug (1410), so the capacity for this question's mug can be filled as 9 oz. The capacity basis comes from the pattern page, not from converting physical dimensions to volume or adopting collector estimates.

## Step 11 · Match bottom row right: round bowl and retain missing values

Evidence observation: Accession number 2010.4.404 D; Size only gives H 8.3 cm and Diam 14.6 cm; Width is not given, and there is no nominal capacity. ## Step 12 · Cross-check common manufacturing fields across the five object pages

Action: Re-check Manufacturer, Place Made, and Date on the five object pages to ensure they are not inferred only from the pattern page.

Evidence observation: All five give Corning Glass Works, Charleroi; United States, PA, Charleroi; 1972–1975. The collection title Snowflake Blue and each Name field serve different roles: Question 1 asks for the pattern name; Question 2 asks for specific object names.

## Step 13 · Check unit boundaries between imperial capacities and metric dimensions

Action: Verify the original writing of cup, pint, quart, and oz in the table, and unify the dimension columns to centimeters as listed officially.

Evidence observation: This question requires nominal capacity and does not require conversion to milliliters; capacity and length/width/height are not the same type. The mug's W 11.3 and Diam 8.8 cannot be merged; for the round bowl, do not infer and fill an unpublished W 14.6 from Diam 14.6. Blank fields are not 0.

## Step 14 · Verify the museum's research system and designer index

Action: Enter the collection/research portal from the Research Room and Pyrex collection overview, then check the Robert Gibson index for the corresponding pattern.

Evidence observation: These pages confirm that the current source uses the Corning Museum of Glass collection and the Pyrex Potluck research system; the Robert Gibson index is associated with Snowflake Blue. ## Step 15 · Use contemporary series materials as corroborating evidence and avoid conflating factory locations

Action: Check Spring Blossom Green, Butterfly Gold, and salt-and-pepper shakers with the same pattern; record separately what each can support.

Evidence observation: The first two patterns provide background on 1972 Compatibles and contemporary object shapes/capacity units; salt-and-pepper shaker 39641 can corroborate Snowflake Blue and 1972–1975, but its manufacturer is Main Plant A Factory and location is NY Corning, not PA Charleroi for the five objects in question.
